findings.description: The dependency review states "The resolved transport uses `rustls` 0.23.46, `aws-lc-rs` 1.18.2, and `aws-lc-sys` 0.46.0" and defers certificate roots to "native platform qualification" (line 38), but it never names the crates that actually determine trust-root and verification behavior in the committed lockfile: rustls-native-certs 0.8.5 with openssl-probe/schannel/security-framework (Cargo.lock:1016-1026), rustls-platform-verifier (Cargo.lock:1039), rustls-webpki 0.103.15, and `ring` 0.17.14, which the graph pulls in through rustls-webpki (Cargo.lock:1066-1072) and quinn-proto (Cargo.lock:857-868). Since this document is the phase-2 record of the network/cryptography dependency selection and its native build boundary, omitting the root-store and verifier path leaves the most security-relevant part of the TLS stack undescribed, and the presence of a second crypto backend (`ring`) alongside aws-lc-rs is not addressed at all.
findings.required_fix: Extend the "HTTP, cryptography, compression, and native code" section with the resolved root-store/verifier crates and their platform FFI, and state explicitly which crypto provider is selected for the SDK's feature set versus merely present in the lockfile (as the document already does for compression backends).

findings.description: `Endpoint::resolve` rejects any path segment containing `%2f`, `%5c`, or `%25` in any case. That is the correct hardening for the traversal finding and is well tested, but it is also a blanket ban on legitimately percent-encoded path data, and no encoding-aware alternative exists: there is no `segment()`/`path_segments()` builder that percent-encodes a caller-supplied value exactly once. Later phases must address resource identifiers and names that can contain `/` or `%` (for example AI profile names, report and scan identifiers reaching the path), and with the current API the only way to send them is to pre-encode, which this check then rejects. docs/FOUNDATION.md:68-72 documents the rejection but offers no supported path-construction route for such values.
findings.required_fix: Add a validated path-segment builder on `RawRequest`/`Endpoint` that percent-encodes each caller-supplied segment once (rejecting separators and dot segments in the decoded value) so encoded identifiers have a supported route, and note it in docs/FOUNDATION.md's transport section.

HMAC byte identity is proven twice and matches the frozen baseline: crates/scm-sdk/src/auth.rs:805-841 asserts the RFC 4231 case-2 digest 5bdcc146…ec3843 with sensitive-marked headers, that no signature is added when no body is present, and that an empty-but-present body is still signed; crates/scm-sdk/src/engine/tests.rs:1307-1345 reads the real loopback socket and asserts the exact body plus an independently computed x-payload-hash. .local/typescript/src/http/auth/api-key.ts:33-45 with utils.ts:37-39 and constants.ts:3-6 confirms identical semantics (Bearer for the token, x-pan-token for the key, hex HMAC-SHA256 whenever bodyText is defined).

OAuth isolation and lifecycle: crates/scm-sdk/src/auth.rs:323-412 stores only a WeakShared refresh with a generation and clear_epoch, so no strong owner survives inside the cache; tests at auth.rs:960-1171 prove deduplication, that a cancelled or deadlined waiter leaves another waiter's refresh running with transport.dropped == 0, that last-waiter drop releases the in-flight HTTP future, that a stale generation cannot evict a newer one, that lifetime is measured from before exchange latency, and that clear() makes an older pending exchange fail with Authentication instead of repopulating the cache. auth.rs:1174-1221 asserts two tenants' caches and formatting are isolated with no issuer URL, client id, secret, token, or tsg scope in Debug output.

Redirects, decompression, replay, and cancellation are proven against real loopback HTTP, not mocks: crates/scm-sdk/src/engine/tests.rs:1347-1384 binds a second listener as the 307 target, asserts (Destination, 307, Rejected), asserts the runtime key appeared only on the original request, and asserts the target never accepted a connection; 1386-1413 shows an 8192-byte payload inside a <128-byte gzip body trips the 128-byte response limit as (Limit, Unknown); 1415-1450 shows a POST whose connection dropped after the server received it is not replayed and reports (Transport, Unknown); 1452-1494 shows cancellation closes the incomplete response and the server observes EOF.

Retry and outcome semantics match docs/FOUNDATION.md:102-109: crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:344-409 retries only when `request.replay_safe` is set, which external callers can only obtain via `RawRequest::read` (engine.rs:46-51, with `safe_read` and `named` pub(crate)); tests at engine/tests.rs:696-912 confirm an arbitrary GET and all POSTs never retry, that 429/502/503/504 retry only for declared reads, that Retry-After 20s exceeds max_retry_delay and is returned to the caller instead of slept, that 401 invalidates the exact generation with zero, one, and shared budgets ([1], [1,2], [2]), and that mutations never replay after 401.
